title: Associated points of a Cohen–Macaulay affine spectrum are component generic points
statement: Let $T$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$, the local ring $T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Cohen–Macaulay, meaning $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For $W=\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and any point $\mathfrak q\in W$, the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $\mathfrak q$ is an associated point of $\mathcal O_W$, meaning that the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{W,\mathfrak q}$ is the annihilator of a nonzero element of that stalk [def-trf-relative-assassin; def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; (ii) $\mathfrak q$ is a minimal prime of $T$, meaning that no prime ideal of $T$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak q$; (iii) $\mathfrak q$ is a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $W$.

source.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), proof, final sentence: associated primes are minimal; expanded using Algebra Tags 0BUS (lemma-CM-ass-minimal-support), 05BV (lemma-ass-minimal-prime-support), and 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass).

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in W$ and put $A=T_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qA$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], $\mathcal O_{W,\mathfrak q}\cong A$ as $T$-algebras. The localization is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Its dimension is a finite integer $e\ge0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension]. Ring isomorphisms carry units, hence maximal ideals, to one another and carry annihilators to annihilators. Thus (i) says precisely that $\mathfrak m$ is an associated prime of the $A$-module $A$. The hypothesis at $\mathfrak q$ says $\operatorname{depth}A=e$.

Assume (i). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-associated-prime-minimal] to the Noetherian local ring $A$ of step 1, its associated prime $\mathfrak m$, and its depth equality (in particular $\operatorname{depth}A\ge e$). It follows that $\mathfrak m$ is minimal in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. If a prime $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ existed in $T$, the inclusion-preserving bijection [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] would give primes $\mathfrak pA\subsetneq\mathfrak qA=\mathfrak m$: strictness follows because contraction is the inverse bijection. This contradicts minimality. Hence (ii) holds.

source.place: Tags 0BUS (lemma-CM-ass-minimal-support), for the local ring as its own module, and 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text: Assume (ii). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-minimal-prime-associated], there is $z\in T$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-localization-depth-zero], there is $w\in A$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_A(w)=\mathfrak qA=\mathfrak m$. Necessarily $w\ne0$, since the annihilator of zero is $A$ and $\mathfrak m$ is proper. The stalk isomorphism established in step 1 transports $w$ and its annihilator to $\mathcal O_{W,\mathfrak q}$ and its maximal ideal. This is (i).

For any prime $\mathfrak p$, its closure is $V(\mathfrak p)$: a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak p$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and then contains all of $V(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], if $\mathfrak q$ is minimal then $V(\mathfrak q)$ is an irreducible component; the closure formula and [def-sc-generic-point] give (iii). Conversely, if $\mathfrak q$ is generic for a component, that component is both $V(\mathfrak q)$ and $V(\mathfrak p)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$. Membership of $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ in these equal sets gives $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so they are equal. Thus (iii) implies (ii), completing all three equivalences.
